sets.g: The other forty Kolbe newspaper hits — and the Settler's eldest son gets a life
sets.n: “DEATH OF COMMANDANT KOLBE”, Grahamstown Journal, 15 April 1868
rows: Grahamstown Journal 1868, second quarter — a hit this archive had already seen and not opened
A FULL OBITUARY FOR JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE

He was two lines in a table: “John Gerson Eliezar ‘Jan’, 1822, Uitenhage”. The obituary gives BORN 7 JULY 1822, MARRIED 3 APRIL 1843 to ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE, DIED 3 APRIL 1868 ON HIS WEDDING ANNIVERSARY at the farm LEEUWBERG, of TYPHUS OR TYPHOID CAUGHT ON COMMANDO. Settled on KAALSPRUIT about 1850. COMMANDANT OF THE DISTRICT, JUSTICE OF THE PEACE, DIRECTOR OF THE BLOEMFONTEIN BANK, DEACON, and a speaker in the VOLKSRAAD in May 1867. THE ROW ABOVE IT IN THE SEARCH RESULTS WAS READ THIS MORNING AND THIS ONE WAS NOT.
A WIDOW AND TWELVE CHILDREN, NOT ONE OF THEM NAMED

Four daughters, only one married, the youngest an infant. TWO SONS HAD SERVED WITH HIM IN THE FIELD and “proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers”. Twelve grandchildren of the 1820 Settler in one household and this archive has none of them. IT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE GAP THE NEWSPAPERS HAVE OPENED.
“THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS”

He said it to the doctor and the others at his bedside; said he had always thought so and had said so in the Raad at the “corn peace” of May 1867; and asked them to RESCIND THEIR RESOLUTION, ANNUL THEIR PROTEST AND TREAT WITH THE GOVERNOR for an equitable boundary. A man dying of a fever he caught fighting that war, asking his own government to give the land back.
And the obituary describes his parents
A CONTEMPORARY CORROBORATION OF THE WHOLE LONDON STORY

“His parents came out with the settlers of 1820; HIS FATHER WAS OF GERMAN EXTRACTION, IF NOT BIRTH, BUT RESIDED AND MARRIED IN LONDON.” This archive built that from a Soho baptism, a London Gazette partnership notice and the 1841 census — none of which the writer of 1868 had in front of him. It also confirms from a fourth direction that the father “became a Missionary to the Griquas at PHILIPPOLIS, and most of his family grew up there”.
The date that does not fit, left not fitting
MARGARET DOWNING “DIED IN BURGHERSDORP ABOUT THREE MONTHS SINCE”

Printed 15 April 1868, which puts her death in JANUARY 1868. This archive has 1867, off her own death notice. A form with a date beats a journalist rounding — but this archive has been caught once already by an estate filed thirteen years after the death it recorded, so the discrepancy is published rather than resolved. HER PLACE OF DEATH IS NEW EITHER WAY: BURGERSDORP, where her husband lies.
Grahamstown Journal, 9 February 1872, quoting the Colesberg Advertiser
“TERRIBLE WARNING” — A KOLBE SUES A WATCHMAKER

An action before the Resident Magistrate between MR. GEO. KOLBE, plaintiff, and MR. T. NELSON, WATCHMAKER, defendant, over a watch entrusted for repair “which, despite repeated promises, the latter neglected to repair or to deliver”. Not a genealogical fact, and kept anyway: it is the only glimpse this archive has of a Kolbe of Colesberg on an ordinary Monday.

sets.g: The newspapers, worked properly — and the Settler's fourth daughter comes back
sets.n: WERDMULLER, ten hits, five of them this family
rows: TEN HITS, AND FIVE OF THEM BUILD A FAMILY

AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, the Settler's fourth daughter, born Graaff-Reinet 1829, has been in this archive as a name with a surname in brackets and nothing else. Her husband is now a man with three dates and a town; her son is named; her son's wife has a death and an obituary; and her granddaughter has a wedding.
THE VON ELGG, PRINTED BY SOMEBODY WHO WAS NOT A GENEALOGIST

“MARRIED at Burghersdorp BY SPECIAL LICENCE, on Tuesday the 7th July 1874, by the Rev. William Cromar, COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER D'ELGG to Miss ELIZABETH JOHANNA CATHARINE VORSTER, both of Burghersdorp.” And it raises a question this archive cannot answer: WAS AUGUSTA LOUISA DEAD BY 1874, or is this a son of the same name?
C.J.O. WERDMULLER IS DEAD, AND HE HAD AT LEAST TWO SONS

“CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER, OF STEYNSBURG. SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER, OF BURGHERSDORP”, married at Wesley Church, Queenstown, to CHARLOTTE ANNE CALLAGHAN, eldest daughter of Hugh Callaghan Esq. of Ashby Manor. A MAN BORN 14 FEBRUARY 1857 — the nameless Burgersdorp baptism found this same morning — WAS TWENTY-SEVEN THAT WEEK. The two finds met in the middle and neither was looking for the other.
DEAD AT THIRTY-TWO, LEAVING TWO LITTLE GIRLS

“DIED — At HOOPSTAD, Orange Free State, on Tuesday, the 17th February, 1891, at the age of 32 years, after a long illness, CHARLOTTE ANNE WERDMULLER … leaving a husband and TWO LITTLE GIRLS to mourn their loss.” A correspondent's obituary adds that she had reached Hoopstad only months before, in indifferent health, with a disorder of the heart that proved organic.
A VICTORIA CROSS MARRIES INTO THE LINE

“MARTINEAU — WERDMULLER — On July 31, at East London, HORACE ROBERT MARTINEAU, V.C., of Durban, to AMY WERDMULLER, SECOND DAUGHTER OF CHARLES WERDMULLER, J.P. OF HOOPSTAD, O.R.C.” She is one of the two little girls of 1891. THIS ARCHIVE PRINTS THE TWO LETTERS AS THE JOURNAL PRINTED THEM and has NOT gone looking for which action he won it for — that is somebody else's page, and borrowing it is exactly the temptation this archive exists to resist.
The link that is not proved, stated rather than smoothed over

If he is the child of 14 February 1857 then Augusta Louisa Kolbe is his mother and Amy is a great-granddaughter of the 1820 Settler. If he belongs to his father's 1874 marriage he is no relation — and a man marrying in 1884 as a SECOND son cannot be. THE DATES FAVOUR KOLBE STRONGLY AND THE DOCUMENTS DO NOT SAY IT. Recorded as a chain with a gap in it.
The search engine will not match a fragment inside D'ELGG. The full surname has to be asked for.

sets.g: G2G answers again — and takes away the only document that names the top of the line
sets.n: Pieter van Zyl and Riël Smit on the 1876 Sterfkennis
rows: The comment, thirteen minutes old when it was read here
HE PREDICTED WHAT IS ON THE PAGE WITHOUT HAVING SEEN THE PAGE

“His real dad, Jan, was already dead for more than 40 years when Petrus Jacobus died… Quite possibly, the informant ‘thought’ the dad's name was G L. I searched for a marriage between a Gerhardus Lodewicus and Magdalena de Beer BUT COULD NOT FIND ONE. If I remember correctly, THERE WAS A CHILD OF PETRUS CALLED GERHARDUS LODEWICUS ON HIS STERFKENNIS.”
Check it against the document this archive has read and photographed
THERE IS. HE IS THE FIFTH CHILD IN LINE 12.

JAN GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS BOOIJSEN. The name this archive takes from LINE 3 for the dead man's FATHER is the back half of his SON'S name, EIGHT LINES BELOW, ON THE SAME SHEET, IN ONE CLERK'S HAND. And the half that gets dropped — JAN — is the name de Villiers gives as the real father, b3c4d7. THE ARCHIVE HAS BEEN LOOKING AT BOTH HALVES FOR WEEKS AND DID NOT PUT THEM TOGETHER.
What it does to the dispute
IT TAKES EVIDENCE AWAY AND ADDS NONE

This is not a proof that the father was Jan, and this archive is NOT swapping one unproved father for another on the strength of a good reading. What it does is REMOVE THE 1876 STERFKENNIS AS DECISIVE EVIDENCE FOR GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS — and line 3 is the only place that name has ever been found. THE OLDEST QUESTION ON THIS SITE JUST GOT HARDER, which is the correct direction for it to move.
Pieter van Zyl's own negative, recorded because it is one
NO MARRIAGE OF A GERHARDUS LODEWICUS TO A MAGDALENA DE BEER

He looked and could not find one. This archive has not repeated the search and records his, attributed. A man who cannot be found marrying the woman his son's death notice gives him is not thereby disproved — but the absence is now on the page.
THE ONLY GERHARDUS IN DE VILLIERS & PAMA (1981) IS b3c1d1 GERHARDUS LORET

“Maybe the Loret changed to Lodevicus over time.” Baptised September 1770, son of Booij — which makes him Petrus Jacobus's FIRST COUSIN and EIGHTEEN YEARS OLD in 1788. He cannot be the father. The suggestion is still worth keeping: it is the only Gerhardus in the printed genealogy at all, and a remembered cousin is exactly the kind of name an informant reaches for.
And the books this archive did not have
PARTS 2 AND 3 ARE ON ARCHIVE.ORG TOO
Riël Smit posted links to all three parts of Oude Kaapsche Familien. This archive downloaded Part 1 on 13 September and never looked for the others. NOT YET READ.

sets.g: The Burgersdorp register, swept image by image — the standing errand of this project
sets.n: 267 images, one of the two missing Barry children, and the reason they were invisible
rows: First, exhaust the index, so the grind is not done for nothing
NINE SEARCHES, ALL RETURNING THE SAME SEVEN CHILDREN

Child surname as BARRY, BERRY, BARRIE, BARY, BARREY, BARRI and BARI — the engine fuzzy-matches, so all seven return one set. Mother as KOLBE, KOLBER and COLBE. And a search on the PARENTS alone — father John, mother Margaretha/Margret/Margaretwina, place Burgersdorp — which returned NOTHING for 1854–1858. THE INDEX ROUTE WAS GENUINELY EXHAUSTED BEFORE A SINGLE IMAGE WAS OPENED.
The film viewer carries an index panel under every image
THIS IS THE TOOL, AND IT WAS THERE ALL ALONG

Film 008039088 — 818 images, not the 534 this archive had written down. Under each image is a table: NAME, BIRTH DATE, PARENT NAME, SECOND PARENT'S NAME, EVENT TYPE, EVENT DATE, EVENT PLACE, for every entry on that page. THE HANDWRITING NEVER HAD TO BE READ. Stepping the viewer and harvesting that table gives about ten entries an image at two and a half seconds each.
Images 338 to 604 — 1853 to 1859, about 2,400 indexed entries
ONE BARRY BAPTISM: CATHERINE MARY SOPHIA, BORN 10 JULY 1855

Image 427. Baptised 22 July 1855 at Burgersdorp, father JOHN BARRY, mother MARGARET LOUISA KOLBE. THE TENTH CHILD. And her sister has the same name: on 25 December 1859 at Dordrecht the same parents baptised another CATHARINA MARY SOPHIA, born 4 August 1859 — the woman who married into the Booyzens. A BAPTISM IS NOT DONE TWICE, so the first child died and the name was given again, which is the ordinary Cape practice. This archive has no burial for her and dates the death only as before August 1859.
WHY NO SEARCH COULD EVER HAVE FOUND HER

The index row for image 427 reads: “ | 10 Jul 1855 | John Barry | Margaret Louisa Kolbe | Baptism | 22 Jul 1855 | Burgersdorp”. THE CHILD IS INDEXED WITH NO NAME AT ALL. Her forenames are written plainly on the page and simply were not keyed. NO SEARCH BY SURNAME, FORENAME OR SPELLING VARIANT CAN RETURN A RECORD THAT HAS NEITHER. The parents are indexed; the child is not. That is a class of invisible record this archive did not know existed, and it is worth more than the one child it produced.
A second nameless row, in the same sweep
THE SETTLER'S FOURTH DAUGHTER HAS A CHILD

Image 513: born 14 FEBRUARY 1857, baptised 10 April 1857 at Burgersdorp, mother AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, father COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER. She is the Settler's daughter born at Graaff-Reinet in 1829, and THIS IS THE FIRST OF HER CHILDREN THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER SEEN. Name column empty again. TWO NAMELESS ENTRIES IN 267 IMAGES AND BOTH BELONG TO THIS FAMILY.

Not at Burgersdorp between 1853 and 1859, and the sweep was complete across that ground. What is left: 1851–1852 before this register opens, the Dordrecht register after 1863, and the real possibility that a child was born and died between two known baptisms and was never entered anywhere.
What the sweep cannot vouch for
ABOUT THIRTY IMAGES RETURNED NO INDEX ROWS

Some of those are genuinely blank pages. This archive cannot say all of them are — the panel may simply not have loaded inside the wait. THE NUMBER IS WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN ROUNDED AWAY, and anyone repeating this should re-visit the zeros.

sets.g: The G2G question was answered — twice, in eighteen hours, by a stranger
sets.n: Pieter van Zyl on estate MHG 10/57
rows: Did anyone answer the post of 13 September?
TWO ANSWERS, BOTH WITHIN EIGHTEEN HOURS, BOTH USEFUL

This archive asked whether the “Form of information of death” cited on WikiTree profile Booyzen-12 was the sterfkennis it has been trying to read since the FamilySearch films started refusing images. THE FORUM WORKED. Two answers, five upvotes each, from PIETER VAN ZYL.
Is the “Form of information of death” the document this archive wants?
NO — AND THAT IS THE ANSWER, NOT A DISAPPOINTMENT

“The Form of Information of a Death or AANGIFTE VAN 'N STERFGEVAL is usually the form that concentrates on the registration of the death by Government. IT DOES NOT USUALLY CONTAIN the information about the spouse's name, parents' names and children. On the other hand the STERFKENNIS or Death Notice gives more information to enable the probate to be processed. It is connected to the will and sent to the Master's office.” SO NOBODY HAS ALREADY READ THE PAGE THIS ARCHIVE WANTS. The letter to Pretoria remains the only route to MHG 10/57, and a week of hoping otherwise is closed in one paragraph by somebody who knows the record series.
What came back that was not asked for
A BAPTISM REGISTER, UPLOADED TO THE PROFILE

Ark 1:1:6KPT-T3Z4, Dutch Reformed Church Registers: HENRY JAMES BOOŸSEN, BORN 12 AUGUST 1887, BAPTISED 27 NOVEMBER 1887, parents WILLEM HERMANUS BOOŸSEN and CATHARINA MARIA SOPHIA BARRY. VERIFIED HERE against the index rather than taken on trust. THE 12 AUGUST 1887 HAS NOW COME FROM A TREE, THEN A GRAVESTONE, THEN A CHURCH REGISTER, IN THAT ORDER — which is exactly backwards, and is how it usually goes.
And a claim this archive has NOT verified
CARPENTER, RETIRED MINER OF LANGLAAGTE ESTATES, DIED OF PHTHISIS

“He was a carpenter when married and a retired miner of Langlaagte Estates when he died of Phthisis.” THIS ARCHIVE HAS CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS, off the Johannesburg burial register it read itself. Phthisis is the Rand miner's disease, and a retired Langlaagte man dying of it in 1956 fits everything else known about him — but the two causes are not the same word, and this archive has read one of the two documents and not the other. RECORDED AS REPORTED AND NOT AS ESTABLISHED. A knowledgeable stranger on a forum is not a document either.
A method note fell out of verifying the ark
THE INDEX MANGLES BARKLY EAST THREE DIFFERENT WAYS IN ONE RESULT SET

One search for the children of Willem Hermanus Booysen returns the same town as “BEAUFORT, Cape Province” (Henry James, 1887), “BARKLY WEST, Cape Province” (a membership entry for the same man, same date), and “BARKLY, QUEENSLAND, AUSTRALIA” (Richard Peter, 1894). THE REGISTER SAYS BARKLY OOST EVERY TIME. Anyone filtering FamilySearch by normalised place for this family will lose most of it, and that is worth knowing before the next sweep.

sets.g: Tolosberg on Jeppe's map of 1899 — the hill three Booyzens were taken on
sets.n: Sheet 6, read at full resolution over twenty-five kilometres
rows: Find a digitised Jeppe 1899 at a resolution that can be read
STANFORD HAS SHEET 6 AS A 75 MB JP2, SERVED OVER IIIF

purl.stanford.edu/jd589rh6196 — “Jeppe's map of the Transvaal or S.A. Republic and surrounding territories”, 16,423 × 24,548 pixels, with a IIIF endpoint that will cut any rectangle at native resolution. Sheet 6 is the SOUTH-EAST sheet, roughly 30.3°–33°E and 25°–28°S, which is exactly the ground. THE MAP IS FREE AND HAS BEEN FREE THE WHOLE TIME.
The Elands River valley, four tiles at native resolution
EVERY FARM IS NAMED AND NUMBERED — AND THERE IS NO TOLOSBERG

Waterval 161, Kindergoed, Elandshoek, Eerste Geluk, Groot Geluk, Nooitgedacht 345, Vlakplaats, Kaalbosch, Schoonspruit, Kietspruit, Weltevreden, Treurfontein, Uitkomst, Doornhoek — and WATERVAL BOVEN and WATERVAL ONDER stations on the Delagoa Bay railway, with GODWAAN STATION to the east. About twenty-five kilometres by twenty, at the scale the surveyor drew it.
Does Jeppe name hills at all? — because a negative is worthless if he does not
HE DOES, AND IN A FORM THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT

MAUCH BG. is printed in italic across a range north of the valley; SPITSKOP, TAFEL KOP, PEERDS KOP, ZWART KOP, ZUIKERBOSCHKOP, SILVERKOP, VAALKOP and BOSCHKOP all appear as named summits. A hill called TOLOSBERG would have been written TOLOS BG. and would have been found. THE TEST IS SOUND AND THE ANSWER IS NO.
IT DOES NOT MOVE THE PIN AND IT DOES NOT BREAK THE SOURCE

The single source for the capture says “Tolosberg in the Waterval Valley, Eastern Transvaal”, and this archive placed the pin at Waterval Boven by inference. Jeppe's silence means the name was LOCAL, or SPELT OTHERWISE, or NEVER A SURVEYED FEATURE — commandos named ground by what they called it, not by what the Surveyor-General called it. The pin stays where it is, still marked as an inference, AND IT IS NOW A TESTED ONE.

sets.g: eGGSA's newspaper extracts — and the Settler's obituary, found in a search that took four minutes
sets.n: Thirty-eight Cape and Natal papers, searched at last
rows: 43 HITS — AND ONE OF THEM IS THE 1820 SETTLER'S DEATH NOTICE IN PRINT

GRAHAMSTOWN JOURNAL, THURSDAY 19 DECEMBER 1844. Eighteen days after he died, four hundred miles from the farm. It gives EIGHT SONS where this archive knew of one, BRUNSWICK SQUARE where the census gives Conduit Street, a man who RENDERED MEDICAL ADVICE TO THE DISTRICT OF COLESBERG FOR MANY YEARS where his own death notice says “Agriculturist”, and a cause of death — an affection on the lungs, after nearly a year ill. IT IS THE RICHEST SINGLE DOCUMENT FOUND IN THIS ARCHIVE IN WEEKS AND IT COST FOUR MINUTES. The collection had been named here as unused for days.
The same notice, tested rather than swallowed
TWO OF ITS FACTS ARE WRONG

It says AGED 44; he was born 7 December 1802 and died 1 December 1844, five days short of forty-two. It says TEN CHILDREN; this archive counts twelve born and one dead in infancy, which leaves eleven. Both are printed on the page beside the find. A newspaper death notice is written by the grieving and set by a compositor four hundred miles away.
FIVE, AND TWO ARE WORTH KEEPING

Eastern Province Herald 1862: “BOOYZEN is a trek-farmer, and was with his brother and brother-in-law digging for water at a place called DEEP FOUNTAIN, within two hours of the ORANGE RIVER” — a Booyzen at work, in a sentence, in 1862. Cape of Good Hope Government Gazette, 1 January 1830: “CHRISTINA BOOYZEN, Widow of WILLEM WOUTER VENTER, aged 79 years, 2 months and 16 days” — born about October 1750, which is older than anything else in this archive. NEITHER IS SHOWN TO BE THIS FAMILY.
SIX, AND ONE IS A MOUNTJOY AT CRADOCK IN 1869

The Friend of the Free State, 1869: “On reaching CRADOCK I found that the Captain was there before me, and had told MOUNTJOY to try and induce me to stay.” Cradock is one of this archive's own places. NOT READ IN FULL, and not connected.
Zero across thirty-eight papers. The surname reached Indwe from Germany and went to the Rand, and it never got into a Cape newspaper column that anyone has transcribed.
ONE, AND IT IS NOT THIS FAMILY
A single hit in The Friend of the Free State, 1859. The ij spelling that dominates this archive's own registers is almost absent from the newspapers.
THE SEARCH BOX IS NOT A FORM

newspapers.eggsa.org runs Geek ElasticSearch: posting the form returns the page and nothing else. The results are drawn by script as you type. It has to be driven as a page — set the value, fire an input event, wait — and not fetched. AN HOUR WAS SPENT POSTING TO AN ENDPOINT THAT WAS NEVER GOING TO ANSWER.

sets.g: The 184 RSA Booyzen documents, enumerated for the first time
sets.n: Seventy-two of them are estates or death notices
rows: NAAIRS · RSA · BOOYZEN, all 184, walked page by page
148 ROWS READ OF 184 — AND THE SHORTFALL IS SAID OUT LOUD

The summary screen pages twenty at a time and this sweep took ten pages. THIRTY-SIX DOCUMENTS WERE NOT REACHED, and this archive is not going to call 148 a complete enumeration. What follows is what 148 rows contain. THE COUNT HAS BEEN QUOTED HERE FOR WEEKS — “184 RSA Booyzen documents” — WITHOUT ANYONE EVER OPENING IT.
Eight gravestones found this morning, looked up in the estate index this afternoon
EIGHT JOINS, FROM TWO COLLECTIONS THAT DO NOT SPEAK TO EACH OTHER

DAVID SCHALK — stone “David S. 1907–1966”, Zandfontein · estate MHG 7653/66. CHARLIE JOHN — stone 1909–1962, Brenthurst · MHG 9371/62. CASPER JOHANNES — stone 1920–1972, Braamfontein · MHG 6160/72. FREDRICK — stone 1899–1970, West Park · MHG 11193/70. ANDRIES ARNOLDUS — stone 1918–1975, West Park · MHG 3100/1975. MARIA CHRISTINA NEE OOSTHUIZEN — stone 1920–1955 · MHG 86/56. WILLEM HERMAN — stone 1946–1965, a boy of nineteen · MHG 1403/1965. JACOBUS FREDRIK JANSE — stone 1939–1957 · MHG 1909/57. EVERY ONE OF THE EIGHT AGREES ON THE YEAR. The stone gives the household name, the index gives the registered name.
The fourth Middelburg stone, the one this archive could not place
SHE HAS A CAPE ESTATE: MOOC 6/9/4898, 54123

“BOOYZEN, CATHARINA JOHANNA HELENA, NEE BEYLEVELD. ESTATE PAPERS. 1937.” Read this morning as an unplaceable stone in the same cemetery as three of this family; by the afternoon she has a file that would name her parents, her husband and her children and settle the question in one page. NOT READ, and it is now near the top of the list.

The woman whose birth date, 8 May 1870, is written beside her name in the Wonderboom deeds register, and whose Rebecca Street stone corrected this archive's reading of that register. Her estate file is MHG 2510/55. NOT READ.
The two oldest Booyzen death notices in the Cape series

MOOC 6/9/30 · 6167 DU PLESSIS, JOHANNA (NEE BOOYZEN), 1843 — already read here, and already established as NOT this family. MOOC 6/9/76 · 4223 BOOYZEN, CORNELIA MARGARIETHA (NEE FOUCHE), 1856 — NOT READ, and older than all but one document in this archive.
MSCE 4064/1974 — BOOYZEN, NICOLAAS THEODORUS. BORN IN WAKKERSTROOM.

The town this archive spent the morning proving its KOLBES moved to. A Booyzen born there is almost certainly a coincidence — Booyzens are everywhere in the Transvaal — and it is recorded as one, because the alternative is to notice it in six months and mistake it for a pattern.
Names this archive has spent the project chasing, on other people's estates

MOOC 6/9/321 · 2120 PRETORIUS, ADRIANA CHRISTINA, NEE BOOYZEN, DEATH NOTICE, 1893 — and Adriana Christina Viljoen is one of the most-linked names in this archive. MHG 5581/64 GROBLER, CATHARINA MARIA SOPHIA, BORN BOOYZEN — the Kolbe name, carried into a fourth surname. NEITHER IS SHOWN TO BE CONNECTED, and both are set down.

sets.g: BARRY, MOUNTJOY and DASCHNER on NAAIRS — the first time these three surnames have been asked
sets.n: The national archives index, all repositories
rows: TWELVE DOCUMENTS — THE WHOLE SURNAME IN SOUTH AFRICA

Two are this archive's own: MHG 1928/42 Joseph Heinrich, and MHG 3734/46 Catherine Mary Sophia born Booyzen. NEW: MHG 2703/63 DASCHNER, WILLIAM HERMAN, and MHG 10287/69 DASCHNER, HEINRICH. The remaining eight are divorce and hire-purchase cases in the Witwatersrand and Transvaal courts, 1949–1980, and belong to a later generation. A SURNAME SMALL ENOUGH TO READ ENTIRE IS A GIFT, and this one was never asked before today.

Including MOOC 6/9/5047 numbers 58379 and 58380 — MOUNTJOY, JAMES JOHN and MOUNTJOY, MARIA LOUISA BERTHA NEE KUMM, CONSECUTIVE NUMBERS, both 1938 — which are the two people on the Barkly East gravestone found this same morning, “MOUNTJOY John James -1937 & Marie Louis -1934”. THE STONE AND THE ESTATE INDEX FOUND EACH OTHER WITHIN THE HOUR, from two collections that do not talk to one another. Also MSCE 600/1974 MOUNTJOY, CHRISTIAN, BORN IN BARKLY EAST, and MSCE 581/1973 SHOOTER, MATHILDA ELIZABETH (BORN MOUNTJOY), BORN IN BARKLY EAST — two Natal estates for people born in this archive's town.

Barry is a forename, a company name, a place and a surname belonging to a large and unrelated Cape family. The index has no date filter and no place filter on the summary screen. IT HAS TO BE PAIRED, and this is recorded as a limit of the method rather than as a negative.
BARRY AND BURGERSDORP · BARRY AND INDWE

The one is a municipality file. Burgersdorp and Indwe hold nothing for this surname in the national index — which is the opposite of what this archive expected, Burgersdorp being where the Barry children were christened.
TWO DOCUMENTS AND BOTH OF THEM MATTER

SAB, VWR 2, B645/8/38, 1937: “AANSOEK DEUR PLAASEIENAAR BARKLY-OOS. RPK BARRY. BYWONER RPK BARRY (SEUN).” A FARM OWNER AND A BYWONER, BOTH R.P.K. BARRY, FATHER AND SON, on one place, with the Department of Social Welfare between them. And NAB, MSCE 2183/1958: “BARRY, HENRY JAMES KOLBE. BORN IN BARKLY EAST, CAPE PROVINCE. UNMARRIED. DECEASED ESTATE.” THE BARRY FORENAME AND THE KOLBE SURNAME IN ONE MAN, born in this archive's town, dying unmarried in Natal. NEITHER FILE IS READ.
A METHOD NOTE — NAAIRS ORs two keywords unless you say otherwise
BARRY WITH BURGERSDORP RETURNED 6,245, WHICH IS MORE THAN BARRY ALONE

The form has a select between each keyword box, defaulting to AND on screen; posted without it, the index ORs them. For an hour this looked like a rich seam. With the operator sent, the same query returns ONE document. A SEARCH THAT RETURNS MORE THAN ITS OWN FIRST TERM IS NOT A SEARCH, and the number should have been the tell.

sets.g: The rest of the Gauteng Booyzen stones, enumerated at last
sets.n: 39 index lines, and five of the twelve Silverton children found
rows: West Park, Braamfontein, Bezuidenhout Park, Brenthurst in Brakpan, Rynsoord in Benoni, Edenvale, Sterkfontein, Panorama in Roodepoort, and in Pretoria: SILVERTON, ZANDFONTEIN, REBECCA STREET, BRONKHORSTSPRUIT and Wonderboom-suid. Five of the thirty-nine were already read here. This is the first time the rest have been listed.
The 1940 estate's eleven children, looked for by their married surnames
FIVE OF THE TWELVE SILVERTON CHILDREN NOW HAVE DATES

BESSIE — “BEKKER Ignatius Michael 1908–1981 & ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA BOOYZEN 1909–1982”, SILVERTON, her parents' own cemetery, and the estate says she married a Bekker. HENNA — “DU PLESSIS Gerhardus Ebenhaezer 1911–1988 & JOHANNA CATHARINA BOOYZEN 1913–1982”, Rebecca Street, and the estate says she married a Du Plessis. FANIE — “BOOYZEN STEPHANUS FRANCOIS 1918–1991 & Elena Jacoba HORN 1921–1989”, Silverton. OUBOET — “BOOYZEN DAVID S. 1907–1966 & Rachel M. 1909–1973”, Zandfontein, born two years after the 1905 marriage. WILLIE — “BOOYZEN Willie 1920–2000 & Enid MOUTON 1926–2000”, Silverton. ALL FIVE ARE MATCHES ON A NAME, A SURNAME-BY-MARRIAGE AND A CEMETERY. NONE IS A DOCUMENT, and all five are entered as inferred.
THE WEAKEST OF THE FIVE, AND SAID SO

The stone gives only the household name — the one thing that cannot tell a son from a nephew. A WILLIE BOSHOFF BOOYZEN 1962–1993 lies in the SAME CEMETERY carrying his grandmother's maiden name, so there is more than one Willie at Silverton. The cemetery fits and the date fits and nothing else does.
The four still missing from the pillar
OUSIE, BETIE, EVERT, PIETIE, JOHAN, HENNIE — six, not four

Susanna Fredrika Aletta, who married a Luus; Beatrix Magdalena Catharina, who married a Vermeulen; Ewert Philippus; Petrus Jacobus; Johan Abraham Frederik; Hendrik Rudolph Philippus. NONE FOUND under a Booyzen stone or under the husband's surname in the Gauteng collection. LUUS and VERMEULEN have not yet been searched, and that is the next errand.
A Booyzen born in 1807, in a family graveyard in Johannesburg
ALREADY IDENTIFIED — AND THIS ARCHIVE FORGOT IT FOR AN HOUR

“VILJOEN J.C.E. nee BOOYZEN 1807-1861”, Bezuidenhout family cemetery. Seeing it in the eGGSA list this archive wrote that it claimed no connection and set it down as a coincidence of three surnames. THAT WAS A REGRESSION. The same stone was worked out days ago from the GEN database: she is JUDITH CORNELIA THERESIA, baptised 16 August 1807, Heese code b3c4d5e6, and she is DAVID SCHALK BOOIJSEN'S FIRST COUSIN — he is b3c4d7e1. Her husband B.C. Viljoen and her daughter Judith Cornelia Etresia Bezuidenhout, born at Graaff-Reinet in 1831, are on the same page of this archive. THE COINCIDENCE OF VILJOEN, BEZUIDENHOUT AND BOOYZEN IN ONE PRIVATE GRAVEYARD IS NOT A COINCIDENCE and this archive had already said so. Left here as written rather than deleted, because an archive that finds the same thing twice and calls it new the second time has a problem worth showing.
Gauteng · LUUS and VERMEULEN — the errand named in the row above, run the same hour

The 1940 estate says Susanna Fredrika Aletta married a LUUS and Beatrix Magdalena Catharina married a VERMEULEN. The Gauteng collection holds about 40 Luus stones and about 40 Vermeulen stones and NOT ONE carries either woman — no Susanna Fredrika Aletta Luus, no Beatrix Magdalena Catharina Vermeulen, under a maiden name or a married one. They did not stay on the Rand, or they are not photographed. OUSIE AND BETIE ARE STILL MISSING, and so are Evert, Pietie, Johan and Hennie.

sets.g: BARRY, MOUNTJOY and DASCHNER on eGGSA — never run before today
sets.n: Three surnames across four provincial collections
rows: A METHOD NOTE FIRST, because it produced four false negatives
THE PROVINCIAL SEARCH SCRIPTS ARE NAMED BY A TWO-LETTER CODE, NOT BY THE PROVINCE

The Eastern Cape posts to /cgi-bin/ecdosearchGraves.pl, and this archive guessed the others by expanding the subdomain — gautengdosearchGraves.pl and so on. EVERY ONE OF THOSE RETURNED NOTHING, and nothing looks exactly like a negative. The real names are ggdosearchGraves.pl, ncdosearchGraves.pl, mpdosearchGraves.pl, read off each province's own form. THE FOUR ZEROES WERE THROWN AWAY RATHER THAN RECORDED. A search you got wrong is not a source that holds nothing.
HUNDREDS, AND ALMOST ALL OF THEM SOMEBODY ELSE'S

The Cape Barrys are a large and well-known family with no shown connection here. The list is not workable by eye and this archive is not going to pretend it worked it. NOT DONE — it needs a date filter or a place filter, and the form has neither.
TWELVE STONES, AND TWO OF THEM AT BARKLY EAST

MOUNTJOY John James -1937 & Marie Louis -1934, and MOUNTJOY Fritz J. 1893–1973 & Aletta J. BRITS 1895–1976, both in BARKLY EAST MAIN CEMETERY — which is this archive's own town. Two more at MIDDELBURG MAIN, the same cemetery as the four Booyzen stones. Also Maclear, East London, King William's Town, Aliwal North. PHOTOGRAPHS LOCATED, NOT YET READ.
TWELVE MORE, AND A KEYS AMONG THEM

“KEYS William H. -1915 & Johanna C. MOUNTJOY -1942” at Krugersdorp Burgershoop. KEYS is a surname this archive has already had to answer a question about. Also KLEYNHANS Petronella C.A. nee MOUNTJOY 1870–1964, MOUNTJOY George 1889–1963 at Brenthurst, and three at WEST PARK, where this family's Johannesburg dead lie. NOT YET READ.
A German surname that arrived at Indwe and went to the Rand; it is not in the Cape collection at all.
SIX, INCLUDING THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN COUPLE

“DASCHNER Joseph Heinrich 1883–1942 & Catherine Mary Sophia BOOYZEN 1891–1946” at West Park, already read. FIVE MORE NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE: Albert Alfred 1962–1964; David and Catherine 1909–1989 at Rynsoord, Benoni; Joseph C. 1911–1992 and Elizabeth H.; Willie 1915–1963 and Millie HARDING; and MARGARET WILHEMINA ELIZABETH JEANETTE DASCHNER 1913–2009, who married a van Jaarsveld — a woman carrying the Barry forenames entire, two generations on.
Mpumalanga · KOLBE — the one this archive did not expect
THIRTEEN, TEN OF THEM AT WAKKERSTROOM

Including BOTH George Augustus Kolbes, their wives, Daan, Freddie, Martha Angeline, Maria Johanna van der Merwe, and three more — Augie, Esther and Cora — on one stone. Plus two at PIET RETIEF: “KOLBE G.A. 1836–1913 & A.M. 1843–1907”, and 1836 is the birth year of the Settler's twin son, born at Burgersdorp. NOT READ; it is the next errand.

“ROUSSEAU ... & MARIA MARGARETHA DOWNING KOLBE 1901–1996” at Zandfontein, Pretoria, and “KOLBE Elizabeth Cathrina 1902–1952 :: KOLBE PETER DOWNING 1972–1976” at Sterkfontein, Krugersdorp — a child of four. THE LONDON SURNAME IS STILL TRAVELLING IN 1972. Also a FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE 1903–1969 at Brenthurst and a GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE 1928–1989 at Primrose: both of this family's Kolbe names still in use on the Rand in the twentieth century.

sets.g: The four Middelburg stones, located a day ago and read today
sets.n: Middelburg main cemetery, eastern Cape
rows: EIGHT STONES, AND NOT ALL OF THEM AT MIDDELBURG

Four at MIDDELBURG main cemetery, which is what this archive came for. But also TWO AT CRADOCK, Deary Avenue — Jan Hendrik 1922–1987 and Yvonne 1926– — and TWO AT HUMANSDORP. Cradock is one of this archive's own places. Those four are not entered as people: one of them has no death date, and this archive does not put a possibly living person on a page.
BOOYZEN Gert Jacobus 1870–1951 — the photograph, read
THE BIRTH CONFIRMED FROM A SECOND SOURCE, THE DEATH NARROWED, AND THE DAY REFUSED

“IN DANKBARE HULDE AAN ONS GELIEFDE VADER EN OUPA — GERT JACOBUS BOOYZEN — GEB. 19 JAN. 1870 — OORL. 2_ AUG. 1951 — SY GENADE WAS VIR MY GENOEG.” 19 JANUARY 1870 is exactly what this archive had, and this is the first source for it that is not the death notice it came from. The death goes from a bare year to AUGUST 1951. THE DAY IS A 2 AND THEN A DIGIT THAT WILL NOT RESOLVE at any magnification, so it is left as a gap rather than guessed at. “VADER EN OUPA” makes him a grandfather, which no document here had said.
BOOYZEN Isabella Fredericka nee COETSEE 1874–1930 — the photograph, read
HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE: 15 APRIL 1874

“TER GEDAGTENIS AAN — ISABELLA FREDERICKA BOOYZEN (GEB. COETSEE) — GEB. 15 APRIL 1874 — OORL. 31 MAART 1930 — HEMELSE RUS.” This archive had “c. May 1874”, worked back from an age on a notice. An exact date cut on a stone beats a month inferred from an age, so the entry moves to 15 April. THE DEATH MATCHES TO THE DAY and is now the THIRD independent source saying 1930 against the 1943 once published here.
BOOYZEN Pieter J. 1904–1937 — the photograph, read
ONE WORD CARRIES THE WHOLE STONE

“HIER RUS — MY GELIEFDE SEUN — PIETER J. BOOYZEN — GEB. 29 DES. 1904 — OORL. 7 JUNIE 1937 — NA DIE KRUIS DIE KROON.” Both dates confirm this archive exactly. THE READING IS IN THE SECOND LINE: “MY geliefde seun”, not “ONS” — ONE surviving parent, not two. His mother had been dead SEVEN YEARS. So his father cut the stone, and then lay down beside them both fourteen years later. THE GRAMMAR OF THE INSCRIPTIONS GIVES THE ORDER THE HOUSEHOLD WENT IN.
BOOYZEN Catharina Johanna Helena nee BEYLEVELDT 1855–1937 — the photograph, read
A FOURTH BOOYZEN IN THE SAME GROUND, AND NO CONNECTION THIS ARCHIVE CAN FIND

“HIER RUS — CATHARINA JOHANNA HELENA BOOYZEN (GEB. BEYLEVELDT) — GEB. 7 JANUARIE 1855 — OORL. 16 MAART 1937.” The Cape Province civil register carries her as BOOYZEN BYLEVELD LANGENBOG BOOYZEN — a chain of surnames that is its own biography — and dates her birth 1857 where the stone says 1855. Her Cape probate names her husband JOHANNES HENDRIK. SHE DIED TWELVE WEEKS BEFORE PIETER J. WENT INTO THE SAME CEMETERY. Same surname, same town, same year: exactly the shape that gets two families welded into one. Written down as a negative rather than left out.

sets.g: The Silverton pillar, matched name by name against the 1940 estate
sets.n: Twelve household names, eleven legal ones — and a twelfth child
rows: Re-read the photograph at four times scale, to be sure of the twelve
OUBOET · OUSIE · BESSIE · BETIE · HENNA · EVERT · ✝BABA · FANIE · WILLIE · PIETIE · JOHAN · HENNIE
Confirmed at magnification. The seventh line carries a BIRTH STAR AND A CROSS and the word BABA, where every other line carries a name.
Set the twelve against the eleven children named on his 1940 estate
EVERY ONE OF THE ELEVEN IS CLAIMED EXACTLY ONCE, AND BABA IS LEFT OVER

Nine go by ordinary Afrikaans diminutive — Bessie←Elizabeth, Betie←Beatrix, Henna←Johanna, Evert←Ewert, Fanie←Stefanus, Willie←Willem, Pietie←Petrus, Johan, Hennie←Hendrik. Two are not names at all: OUBOET is eldest brother and OUSIE eldest sister, and they fall to David Schalk, who heads the estate list, and to Susanna Fredrika Aletta, the one daughter the diminutives leave. NOTHING IS UNASSIGNED EXCEPT BABA. THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE TWELFTH CHILD REAL: not the count, but the fact that the count has nowhere else to go.
The weak link, named rather than hidden
Henna can stand for Hendrina as readily as for Johanna. There is no Hendrina on the estate, which is why the match is made — but it is the one of the nine that rests on an absence.
Does the archive have this shape already?
YES, ONCE — AND IT IS THE SAME LESSON

Joseph Heinrich Daschner's 1942 death notice named ELEVEN children; the Brixton burial register produced a TWELFTH, George Downing Daschner, three months and five days old, buried 1925. A DEATH NOTICE LISTS THE LIVING. A GRAVESTONE, CUT BY THE FAMILY, LISTS THE CHILDREN. Two documents of different kinds, and the difference between them is worth more than either alone.
Baba's birth date, sex, name or order

The stone gives a star, a cross and a word that means baby. This archive enters the child under that word and claims nothing else. A Pretoria burial register or the Silverton cemetery register would be the next place to look, and neither has been searched.

sets.g: Wakkerstroom proved a second time — not by a name but by a household
sets.n: Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe's eight children
rows: q.surname=Kolbe · q.givenName=Angeline · South Africa — the errand as set
ANGELINE KOLBE, AGED 28, DIED WAKKERSTROOM 15 NOVEMBER 1900

The record is thin and honest about it: female, surname Kolbe, aged 28 years, died 15 Nov 1900 at Wakkerstroom, registered in the Transvaal civil deaths. NO PARENTS, NO HUSBAND, NO CAUSE. SHE IS NOT THE VOLKSRUST CAMP GRAVE the errand asked her to be reconciled with — that is a G.E. Kolbe aged 35, and Angeline is 28, a year earlier, in a different town, when the Volksrust camp was barely open. THE RECONCILIATION FAILS, and the right answer is that they are two women.
AND A SIXTY-DAY-OLD CHILD AT VOLKSRUST

MARTHA ANGELINE KOLBE, born 9 October 1901, died 8 December 1901, buried at VOLKSRUST. Age on the civil death register: 0. She lived sixty days and every one of them was inside the war. Volksrust held a concentration camp. This archive has read no camp register naming her and so records the burial place and not the cause — but it will not pretend the date is a coincidence either.
q.surname=Kolbe · q.fatherGivenName=Frederik Fortunatus — ask the index for a FATHER, not a person
EIGHT CHILDREN, AND A WIFE THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW EXISTED

FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE, the Settler's tenth child, born at Bethulie in 1839, married ELIZABETH JOHANNA DU TOIT. Their children are baptised at COLESBERG in 1863, 1865, 1868, 1873, 1876 and 1877; at HOPETOWN in 1870; and at BETHULIE in 1881, which is his own birthplace forty-two years on. The eldest is a GEORGE AUGUSTUS, named for a grandfather nineteen years dead. This archive had held Frederik Fortunatus as a name and a date of birth and nothing else. The relationship search is what opened him.
The eldest son, followed to the far end
GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE — COLESBERG 1863 TO WAKKERSTROOM 1954, AGED 91

Baptised Colesberg 11 Oct 1863, born 29 July. Died Wakkerstroom 28 September 1954, aged 91 — AND 29 JULY 1863 TO 28 SEPTEMBER 1954 IS EXACTLY 91. Married MARTHA SOPHIA KLOPPER, aged seventeen, about 1885; she died 14 Oct 1950 aged 83. A PRISONER OF WAR IN 1902, aged 40, residence Wakkerstroom — the fourth man in this archive taken in that war and the only one who is not a Booyzen. His daughter Maria Johanna's 1953 estate file names the household outright: father George Augustus Kolbe, mother Martha Sophia Klopper.
q.surname=Kolbe · q.anyPlace=Wakkerstroom, read against the Colesberg fonts
THREE OF THE EIGHT ARE IN THE EASTERN TRANSVAAL

MARGARET HARRIET, baptised Hopetown 1870, marries Dirk Jacobus Aspheling van der Spuy at Wakkerstroom aged 24. ELIZABETH JOHANNA, baptised Colesberg 1876, marries John Charles Pattison at Wakkerstroom aged 21. Both ages agree with the font to the year. WITH THEIR BROTHER THAT IS THREE OF EIGHT, FOUR HUNDRED MILES FROM WHERE THEY WERE CHRISTENED. Yesterday the convergence was proved by a name — Frederik Fortunatus DOWNING Kolbe, a London surname in the Transvaal. THIS IS THE BETTER PROOF: a name can be coincidence, a family moving cannot.
THE INDEX MANGLED THE LINE THAT PROVES THE DESCENT

His death registration carries a relationship where a name should be: “G A Kolbe's son”, which the index has read as a surname and printed as “G A KOLBELSSON”. That misprint is what ties the two 1918 graves — Daan, 19 June, aged 25, and Freddie, 2 November, aged 27 — to the old man who outlived them by thirty-six years. FOUR MONTHS APART IN 1918 IS THE INFLUENZA.
q.surname=Kolbe · q.givenName=George Augustus, all of them
AT LEAST TWO MEN OF THAT NAME IN THE TRANSVAAL AT ONCE — AND THIS IS A WARNING, NOT A FIND

One born COLESBERG 1863, dead Wakkerstroom 1954 aged 91. One born BURGERSDORP 1861, dead Standerton 8 November 1934 aged 73 — Burgersdorp being where the Settler is buried and where his twin son George Augustus was born in 1836. A third George Augustus, aged 27, marries SUSANNA MARGARETHA SWART in the Free State register with residence given as Wakkerstroom, and THIS ARCHIVE CANNOT SAY WHICH MAN THAT IS. A “Susanna Margaretha DOWNING Kolbe” also stands in the Transvaal probate index — a second carrier of the London surname, unattached. Set down so that nobody later merges two men into one.
THE MARRIAGE, AND HER OWN DEATH

“George Augustus Kolbe and Martha Sophia Klopper”, Transvaal civil marriages 1870–1931, the bride aged 17 and born 1868. And “Martha Sophia Klopper Kolbe”, born 1867, died 14 October 1950 aged 83. SHE IS THE FOURTH BRIDE IN THIS ARCHIVE MARRIED BEFORE EIGHTEEN, and the third in the Kolbe line — after Margaret Downing at fifteen and the Settler himself at sixteen.
Volksrust camp register, for Martha Angeline Kolbe

The burial is indexed from BillionGraves, not from a camp register. Until a camp register is read this archive records that a two-month-old was buried at Volksrust in December 1901 and does not write the word camp into her entry. The register is the next errand.
Angeline Kolbe, against the eight Colesberg fonts

Aged 28 in November 1900 puts her birth near 1872. Martha Angelina was born January 1868 and Catharina Maria Louisa July 1873; neither is 28 in 1900. She is most likely a daughter-in-law, married into the surname. THIS ARCHIVE WILL NOT GUESS WHICH SON.
The POW record itself, read rather than indexed — ark 1:2:4126-8XTJ
WO 108/368 — AND IT TAKES BACK WHAT IT GAVE

The full entry: GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, AGE 40, NATIONALITY TRANSVAALER, RESIDENCE WAKKERSTROOM, PRISON NATAL, event 1902, from “List of Boer prisoners of war, numbers 1-32561, 1899-1902”, WO 108/368 at The National Archives. HELD IN NATAL, not shipped — unlike the three Booyzens taken at Tolosberg, who sailed on the City of Cambridge. The residence is what made this archive claim him for the Colesberg-born man. THE AGE UNMAKES IT: he was 39 in 1902, and the Burgersdorp-born George Augustus of 1861 was 40. Withdrawn to /corrections/ the same hour it was published.

sets.g: The entity audit — sweeping for other things that travel through data
sets.n: An arrow entity printed at the reader on the home page
rows: Sweep the 642 built pages for a double-escaped entity

The bug the reader caught: three way-in cards on the home page passed their arrow as a DATA STRING — the arrow written as an HTML entity, ampersand r-a-r-r semicolon — and a string prop is escaped on output, so the page printed those five characters where an arrow belonged. Arrows written straight into markup were never affected. Having fixed the three, this sweep asks the built site whether the same fault is anywhere else. IT IS NOT.
Ask the same of the source rather than the output — every entity sitting inside a quoted prop or data value in site/src
NO ENTITY ANYWHERE ELSE IN PROP OR DATA POSITION

The source is asked as well as the output, because a page can exist without having been rebuilt. 429 em dashes, 306 arrows, 244 middots, 85 right single quotes, 74 en dashes and 69 right double quotes are in use across the site as entities, and every one of them is in markup, where escaping never touches it.
Every file in site/src/data, for an entity written into data

people.js, places.json, searched.json, corrections.json and the rest are clean, which is the root of it — the home page's three cards were the only place an entity had been written into something that would later be escaped.
Then: a check in tools/drift.py, so it cannot come back
THE BUILD NOW FAILS ON A DOUBLE-ESCAPED ENTITY

The check reads the built pages, not the source, so it catches the SYMPTOM whatever the cause — an escaped entity reaching a reader is a bug no matter which prop or which component put it there. It is absolute, with no exception for a page that means to quote one; this page wanted to and spells the arrow out in words instead, because a check with an exception is a check that will be excepted. Tested by planting one in the built home page: the build failed and named both the entity and the page. THE READER FOUND THIS ONE BEFORE THE BUILD DID, WHICH IS THE WRONG WAY ROUND, and that is what the check is for.

sets.g: Wakkerstroom PROVED — a man who carries both family names
sets.n: Frederik Fortunatus DOWNING Kolbe
rows: Born 1891 at WAKKERSTROOM, died there 2 NOVEMBER 1918, Transvaal probate 1918. HE CARRIES BOTH OF THIS FAMILY'S KOLBE NAMES AT ONCE. FREDERIK FORTUNATUS is the Settler's son, whom this archive already calls “the source of the Fortunatus name across three families”. DOWNING is MARGARET DOWNING, whom George Augustus Kolbe married at St Leonard's Shoreditch in 1819 — a London surname with no business in the eastern Transvaal except through that marriage. One man, born seventy-two years after the wedding, carrying both. THE CONVERGENCE IS NO LONGER A CONVERGENCE; the Wakkerstroom Kolbes are this family's Kolbes.

Every stone found this morning now has a record behind it. DANIEL JAKOBUS KOLBE, born 1893, died 19 JUNE 1918 at Wakkerstroom — the stone's “Daan 1893-1918”. FREDERIK FORTUNATUS DOWNING KOLBE, died 2 NOVEMBER 1918 — the stone's “Freddie -1918”. TWO YOUNG MEN OF ONE FAMILY DEAD FOUR MONTHS APART IN 1918, which is the influenza. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, born 1863, died 28 SEPTEMBER 1954 — the stone's 1863-1954, and his wife MARTHA SOPHIA KLOPPER is named as the mother of MARIA JOHANNA KOLBE, born 1886 at Wakkerstroom, died 1 October 1953, who is the “van der Merwe née Kolbe” stone. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE born 1861 married SUSANNA MARGARETHA SWART — the 1861-1934 stone. And MARGARET HARRIET KOLBE, born 1871, married DIRK JACOBUS ASPELING VAN DER SPUY — the Utrecht stone found through NAAIRS yesterday.
A war death and a war record

ANGELINE KOLBE, born 1872, DIED AT WAKKERSTROOM ON 15 NOVEMBER 1900 — in the middle of the war, in a district that had a concentration camp at Volksrust twenty miles away, and NAAIRS's gravestone data holds a “GE KOLBE, died between 1899 and 1901, aged 35” in that camp cemetery. Not the same person on the figures, and the first time a woman of this surname has been found dying in that district in those years. And GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, born 1862, resident WAKKERSTROOM, with a MILITARY record of 1902 — neither read.
What this does to the Colesberg question
It says where the children went

George Augustus Kolbe, the 1820 Settler, died at Wurtemburg, Colesberg, in 1844 leaving nine children, and this archive loses sight of most of them. THIS IS WHERE A BRANCH WENT: north-east to the Transvaal–Natal border, to Wakkerstroom and Piet Retief, taking FORTUNATUS, GEORGE AUGUSTUS and DOWNING with them, and still using all three seventy years later. NO INDIVIDUAL IS YET ADOPTED into the family: no document read names the Settler as their ancestor, and the estates that would — NAB MSCE 2032/1969 and 965/1956 — are Pietermaritzburg files past the 1950 close of the filmed Natal probate series.

sets.g: The Cape genealogical codes, resolved — and G2G answers back twice more
sets.n: a cousin identified, a father-candidate offered, and a reply this archive cannot post
rows: b3c4d5e6, resolved from the volume already downloaded
A FIRST COUSIN OF DAVID SCHALK

The gravestone at Bezuidenhout Park, Johannesburg, reads “JCE VILJOEN, NEE BOOYZEN, born 02-07-1807, died 11-12-1861”, citing Heese as b3c4d5e6. Walked in de Villiers 1893, which this archive downloaded this morning: b3 = GERRIT, married Johanna Durand 1733; c4 = JAN, baptised 29 January 1741; d5 = JAN JONATHAN, baptised 11 July 1779, married 28 May 1797 to JUDITH CORNELIA THERESIA VILJOEN; and e6 = “JUDITH CORNELIA THERESIA, GEDOOPT 16 AUGUSTUS 1807”. Born 2 July, baptised 16 August — six weeks, exactly right. SHE IS THE ARCHIVE'S DAVID SCHALK BOOIJSEN'S FIRST COUSIN: he is b3c4d7e1, she is b3c4d5e6, both grandchildren of Jan. She married a Viljoen, as her mother was one, and lies in Johannesburg.

“On the Booijsen side (page 78 of Kaapsche Familien part 1): B3 Gerrit B x Johanna du Rand. B3C4 Jan B x Magdalena de Beer. B3C4D7 PETRUS JACOBUS B BAPTISED 21 SEPT 1788 x ANNA MARIA V D MERWE.” That is this archive's own reading of the page, arrived at separately and stated in the same notation. Riël Smit added the archive.org links for all three parts.
G2G answer 3 · Riël Smit — and it goes straight at Question 0

“The only Gerhardus Booysen in DE VILLIERS & PAMA (1981) is B3C1D1 GERHARDUS LORET (BOOIJSEN) BOOYSEN, baptised Sep 1770 in Drakenstein. Maybe the LORET changed to LODEVICUS over time.” This archive found that man in the 1893 text without knowing what to do with him — “Gerhardus Loret, gedoopt 16 September 1770”, a son of BOOIJ Booijsen and Magdalena du Plessis. TWO THINGS FOLLOW AND THEY PULL OPPOSITE WAYS. It is a genuine candidate for the name on the 1876 Sterfkennis, offered by a senior member from the revised 1981 edition this archive has never seen. BUT HE IS b3c1d1 — a son of BOOIJ, not of JAN — so he is Petrus Jacobus's FIRST COUSIN, not his father, and at eighteen in 1788 he is a poor fit for it besides. The likeliest reading is that the 1876 informant reached for a remembered family name and attached it to the wrong man.
The reply this archive owes them

A reply is drafted in substance and cannot be posted: the WikiTree session has expired and the page offers only Log In. What it should say — that the book was downloaded and read, that b3c4d7 matches independently, that b3c4d5e6 resolves to Judith Cornelia Theresia and settles a Johannesburg gravestone, and ONE QUESTION WORTH ASKING THEM: does de Villiers & Pama (1981) still put Petrus Jacobus under JAN, or did the revision move him? That is the whole of Question 0 in a sentence, and a member with the 1981 edition open could answer it in a minute.

sets.g: The Wakkerstroom convergence, tested
sets.n: Frederik Fortunatus is the thread, and it holds
rows: Booysens and Booyzens are at Wakkerstroom as well as Kolbes: Nicolaas Gerhardis Franscoas 1866–1943, Pieter Jacobus 1890–1960, J.S. 1900–1983, Magritha Cornelia née v.d. Merwe 1898–1938, Jacobus G. 1929–1968, Nicolaas Gerhardis Francois 1919–1938, Daniel Johannes Andries Booyens 1917–1995, and one with the z — JOHANNES STEPHANUS BOOYZEN 1922–1995. Forename-resonance only; BOOYSEN and PIETER JACOBUS are far too common to argue from, and nothing here is claimed.
SIXTEEN DOCUMENTS, AND THE RARE NAME IS IN THEM

The Booysen side proves nothing; the KOLBE side does much better. (1) NAB CSO 1908/4469: “C K BARRY, WAKKERSTROOM. MR. G S KOLBE ASKS TO BE SUPPLIED WITH A COPY OF THE ROAD BOARD LAW” — A BARRY AND A KOLBE IN ONE DOCUMENT AT WAKKERSTROOM, which are precisely the two surnames joined by the 1846 marriage at the head of this archive's Kolbe line. (2) NAB PVS 2644/1912: “FF KOLBE — permission to move one bull from Wakkerstroom to Saxony, Utrecht”. (3) NAB MSCE 2032/1969: “KOLBE, FREDERIK FORTUNATUS HOFMEYR. BORN IN NAAUWPOORT, WAKKERSTROOM”, deceased estate, wife born Badenhorst. (4) NAB MSCE 965/1956: “KOLBE, HENDRIK JOHANNES HOFMEYR. BORN IN WAKKERSTROOM”. (5) SAB CEN E1573, 1911–1913: “GA KOLBE, WAKKERSTROOM” — which sits exactly on the Piet Retief gravestone of G.A. KOLBE 1836–1913.
What the convergence actually rests on

Not the place and not the Booysens — the NAME. This archive already calls Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe “the source of the Fortunatus name across three families”, and it is a son of GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, the 1820 Settler. FORTUNATUS IS NOT A NAME THAT TURNS UP TWICE BY ACCIDENT. It is at Wakkerstroom in 1912 and again on an estate for a man born at Naauwpoort in that district. Beside it sits GEORGE AUGUSTUS, on three separate stones there and at Piet Retief, and a Barry in the same 1908 file. TAKEN TOGETHER THE WAKKERSTROOM KOLBES ARE ALMOST CERTAINLY THIS FAMILY'S KOLBES, a generation or two on from Colesberg. NOT PROVED: no document yet read names the Settler as their ancestor, and none has been adopted. The test that would settle it is estate MSCE 2032/1969 or 965/1956, either of which should name parents.

sets.g: The last two provinces — Northern Cape and Mpumalanga
sets.n: Colesberg is bare; the Kolbe name is not
rows: “KOLBE George 1930-2000 & Bettie 1923-2003”, De Aar new cemetery. That is the entire Kolbe presence in the photographed Northern Cape collection. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE DIED AT THE FARM WURTEMBURG, COLESBERG, ON 1 DECEMBER 1844, and the memorial of 1839 puts him on KNAP DAAR in the same district. Neither farm, and no stone of his, is in the collection.
193 stones, two at Colesberg, neither ours

The province holds 193 Booy-family stones, overwhelmingly at Upington, Postmasburg, Hartswater and De Aar. COLESBERG ITSELF HAS TWO: Lewiesa Booyse, 1957–2011, and Helena Booysens, born 1931, on a Marais stone — both modern, both in the cemetery beside the N1. THE COLESBERG COVERAGE IS THIN, and the district where this family's Kolbes farmed in the 1830s and 1840s is effectively unphotographed. A clean negative with its reason attached.
Thirteen stones, and the name three more times

Twelve of the thirteen are at WAKKERSTROOM and PIET RETIEF, on the Transvaal–Natal border — a Kolbe community this archive did not know existed. And THE NAME IS THERE THREE TIMES OVER: “KOLBE G.A. 1836-1913 & A.M. 1843-1907” at Piet Retief; “KOLBE GEORGE AUGUSTUS 1861-1934 & Susanna Margaretha 1861-1940” at Wakkerstroom; and “KOLBE GEORGE AUGUSTUS 1863-1954 & Martha Sophia KLOPPER 1867-1950”, also Wakkerstroom. This archive's George Augustus Kolbe was the 1820 Settler, born 1802 and dead at Colesberg in 1844; these three are born 1836, 1861 and 1863. Also there: P. J. Kolbe 1865–1919, Martha Angeline 1901–1901, and DAAN 1893–1918 with FREDDIE, also 1918 — two young men dead in the influenza year. NONE IS CLAIMED. What is claimed is that the forename travelled, as Margaret Downing's did.
Volksrust camp cemetery, looked for and not found here
In the index, not in the photographs

NAAIRS's GEN database gives “GE KOLBE, died between 1899 and 1901, aged 35, Concentration Camp cemetery, Volksrust”. That stone does NOT appear among the thirteen Kolbe records in eGGSA's photographed Mpumalanga collection. The two bodies of data are the same society's work from different doors, and they do not hold the same things — worth knowing before either is treated as complete.

FamilySearch's full-text search returned, among its South African collections, “VOTERS' LIST (MALE) 1931 — WAKKERSTROOM” for the surname BOOYZEN. The gravestones now put a KOLBE community in the same small border town. Booyzens and Kolbes at Wakkerstroom is either coincidence or the family, and nobody has tested which.

sets.g: Gauteng gravestones — the Johannesburg and Pretoria family, photographed
sets.n: 640 stones, 38 spelt with a z, and five of this archive's people among them
rows: The archive has read ten Johannesburg burial REGISTERS and had a photograph of none of those graves. The Gauteng collection holds thirty-eight Booyzen-spelt stones across West Park, Braamfontein, Bezuidenhout Park, Brenthurst in Brakpan, Rynsoord in Benoni, Edenvale, Sterkfontein, Panorama, and four Pretoria cemeteries — Silverton, Zandfontein, Rebecca Street and Bronkhorstspruit.
Four stones that are certainly this family

“BOOYZEN STEFANUS FRANCOIS 1874-1940” and “BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA NEE BOSHOFF 1889-1977”, a joint stone at SILVERTON, PRETORIA — he died at East Lynne in 1940 and she is given a death year for the first time. “BOOYZEN HENRY JAMES 1887-1956” at WEST PARK. “BOOYZEN JOHN BARRY 1884-1952” at BRENTHURST, BRAKPAN — this archive had him as “c. 1884” with NO DEATH AT ALL and an estate number, MHG 769/52, on a film that will not open; the stone supplies both the year and the town. And “DASCHNER JOSEPH HEINRICH 1883-1942 & CATHERINE MARY SOPHIA” at WEST PARK — the Indwe marriage, on one stone, in Johannesburg.
A fifth stone that closes a loop

“BOOYZEN PETRUS JACOBUS 1873-1947 & MAGDALENA JOHANNA BEZUIDENHOUT”, REBECCA STREET CEMETERY, PRETORIA. Two threads from earlier today meet on it. The Wonderboom South transfer register names “Boedel wyle P. J. Booyzen” passing to “MAGDALENA JOHANNA BOOYZEN”, and “M. J. BOOYZEN, BORN BEZUIDENHOUT, widow” — a couple this archive could not identify. And the prisoner register gives PETRUS JACOBUS BOOYZEN, aged 27, of Pretoria, taken at Tolosberg on 25 April 1901, which puts his birth about 1874. A Petrus Jacobus Booyzen born 1873 and buried at Pretoria with a wife born Bezuidenhout fits both. STRONG AND NOT PROVED — the stone names no parents.
And two confirmations of other people's work
WikiTree and NAAIRS both hold up

“BOOYZEN WILLEM HERMANUS 1925-1996 & CYNTHIA ROSALIND 1927-” at RYNSOORD, BENONI is WikiTree's Booysen-831, which gives him born 25 October 1925 and married to Cynthia Rosalind Hoeftman at Johannesburg in 1955. And “VILJOEN J.C.E. NEE BOOYZEN 1807-1861” at BEZUIDENHOUT PARK is the stone NAAIRS's GEN database produced this morning from the other direction. Neither is claimed for this family; both show the sources agreeing.
The six photographs, downloaded and read
Every one gave more than its index line

The gallery serves an HTML wrapper at the .JPG address; the image itself is at a /cache/ path inside it, and fetching that with a referer works. SIX STONES READ. Stefanus Francois Booyzen — born 29 SEPTEMBER 1874, not “about October”, on a double stone at Silverton whose centre pillar lists TWELVE CHILDREN by household name, one marked dead. John Barry Booyzen — 26 APRIL 1884 to 23 JANUARY 1952, where this archive had “c. 1884” and no death at all. Henry James Booyzen — GEB. 12.8.1887, putting on a gravestone the date this archive had marked as coming from WikiTree and not from a document. Catherine Mary Sophia Daschner, BORN BOOYZEN with the z, born 22 APRIL 1891 exactly as her Barkly Oost baptism says, died 14 July 1946; her husband Joseph Heinrich Daschner, 27 December 1883 to 19 April 1942. And Petrus Jacobus Booyzen, 29 May 1873 to 25 March 1947, with MAGDALENA JOHANNA BOOYZEN GEB. BEZUIDENHOUT, GEB. 8 MEI 1870 — which is the number written beside her name in the Wonderboom deeds register, and identifies her beyond doubt. IT ALSO FORCED A CORRECTION: she was widowed in 1947, so the 1907 date read off that ledger row was a column mis-alignment, and is withdrawn.

sets.g: eGGSA's gravestone photographs — and two of this family are in them
sets.n: a couple known only from estate files, now with stones
rows: How the graves site is organised

graves.eggsa.org is only a front door. The collection is split by province, each with its OWN SUBDOMAIN AND ITS OWN SEARCH, and there is no way to search all of them at once — the site says so itself. For this family: graveseastcape (Graaff-Reinet, Cradock, Middelburg, Barkly East, Dordrecht, Indwe), gravesnortherncape (Colesberg), gravesgauteng (Johannesburg, Pretoria), gravesmpumalanga (Volksrust). The Eastern Cape search is a CGI form at /Search/ecsearchGraves.htm posting to /cgi-bin/ecdosearchGraves.pl, and it works.
203 stones, eight spelt with a z

Most are Booyens and Booysen families with no connection here. Filtering to the Z SPELLINGS leaves eight, and FOUR OF THEM ARE IN ONE CEMETERY — MIDDELBURG MAIN CEMETERY: Catharina Johanna Helena née Beyleveldt 1855–1937, GERT JACOBUS 1870–1951, ISABELLA FREDERICKA NÉE COETSEE 1874–1930, and Pieter J. 1904–1937.
BOOYZEN Gert Jacobus 1870–1951 · BOOYZEN Isabella Fredericka nee Coetsee 1874–1930

Gerrit Jacobus Booÿsen was born 19 JANUARY 1870, the only child on his father's 1884 death notice, and he married ISABELLA FREDERIKA COETSEE AT MIDDELBURG on 23 March 1896. His estate is TAB MHG 5155/51 — a 1951 file this archive has never been able to read because the film returns 403. THE STONE GIVES HIM 1870–1951. Hers gives 1874–1930, which matches her own death notice and independently confirms this archive's correction that she died in 1930 and was simply not reported until 1943. They married at Middelburg and they are buried at Middelburg, a few stones apart. PHOTOGRAPHS LOCATED AND NOT YET READ: the inscriptions may carry more than the index line does.

sets.g: eGGSA's newspaper extracts — the right country's papers, opened
sets.n: a usable method, four quarters swept, and a site that has just moved
rows: The addresses, which have all just changed

eggsa.org/newspapers/ now returns 404 and so does every deep link Google still holds for it. The collections have moved to SUBDOMAINS: NEWSPAPERS.EGGSA.ORG for the newspaper extracts and GRAVES.EGGSA.ORG for the gravestone photographs. Recorded first because anyone following an older citation will conclude the resource is gone, and it is not.
The search, which does not work

The site runs a Geek ElasticSearch widget that does not respond to a form POST or to scripted input, and Joomla's own com_search is not installed — /index.php?option=com_search returns “Component not found”. THE CONTENT IS STILL REACHABLE: each newspaper has a page, each page lists its quarters, and each quarter is a single full-text transcription of ten to eighteen thousand characters that can be fetched and read straight through. That is the method, and it works.

Titles include the CAPE FRONTIER TIMES, CAPE OF GOOD HOPE GOVERNMENT GAZETTE, CAPE TIMES, DAILY REPRESENTATIVE, EASTERN PROVINCE HERALD, FORT BEAUFORT ADVOCATE, GRAHAMSTOWN JOURNAL, QUEENSTOWN FREE PRESS — and the GRAAFF-REINET HERALD, transcribed by Sue Mackay from CO53/43 at the National Archives, Kew, covering 1852 to 1856 in ten quarters. Graaff-Reinet is where this family is oldest and where its baptisms run from 1788 to 1857.
Graaff-Reinet Herald · 1852 Oct–Dec, 1853 Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep

Fetched and read in full for BOOY, BOOIJ, KOLBE, MOUNTJOY, MONTJOY and VILJOEN. NOT ONE OCCURRENCE across roughly 55,000 characters of advertisements, notices and reports. A scoped negative and a small one: four quarters of ten, in one paper of twenty, in a five-year window. What it establishes is that the method works and the reading can be trusted — the transcriptions are genuine running text, not indexes.

sets.g: Gravestones — NAAIRS's GEN database, and eGGSA
sets.n: a camp death, a name carried eighty years, and the right newspapers at last
rows: The Genealogical Society's gravestone data, reached through NAAIRS rather than eGGSA. Three stones at the BEZUIDENHOUT FAMILY CEMETERY, Bezuidenhout Park, Johannesburg, recorded by P Holden in 1989 — and the Booyzen is in the inscriptions, not the surnames. “JCE VILJOEN, NEE BOOYZEN. Born 02-07-1807. Died 11-12-1861. Wife of BC Viljoen” — cited to JA HEESE, SOUTH AFRICAN GENEALOGIES, CODE b3c4d5e6. Her husband BC Viljoen, 1807–1859, is cited to de Villiers and Pama as b3c4d2e11f4. And their daughter JUDITH CORNELIA ETRESIA BEZUIDENHOUT, née Viljoen, was BORN 30 OCTOBER 1831 AT GRAAFF-REINET and died at Doornfontein in 1904. NOT ADOPTED: a Booyzen woman born July 1807 cannot be a sister of David Schalk, baptised January 1807, so she is a cousin at best. But she is of his generation, at his parish, and she has a HEESE CODE — the second time in two days a source has pointed at Heese with a number attached.
A camp death, and a name that lasted eighty years

Four stones. Two matter. FIRST: “GE KOLBE. Died between 1899 and 1901. Aged 35 years.” — CONCENTRATION CAMP CEMETERY, VOLKSRUST. Question 3 asks whether this family's women and children were in a camp and answers “searched, and not found” — but that search was run on BOOYZEN against a database built largely from camp death lists. Here is a KOLBE of thirty-five dead in a camp. Not this archive's person on any evidence yet, and the first camp death to touch any of its surnames. SECOND: “MARGARET or MARGARIT DOWNING FOURIE, NEE KOLBE. Born 29-09-1899. Died 08-12-1979” — New Gelderland Cemetery, Lower Tugela, Natal, recorded twice by different compilers. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE MARRIED MARGARET DOWNING AT SHOREDITCH IN 1819. Eighty years later a Kolbe girl is christened MARGARET DOWNING KOLBE, and she is buried in Natal in 1979. Also: Margaret Harriet van der Spuy, née Kolbe, died Utrecht 1946.
eGGSA — and the newspapers this family is actually in
The Cape papers, not the British ones

The photo library did not surface a Booyzen stone for Graaff-Reinet, Cradock or Colesberg on the searches run. What it did surface is a resource this archive has never touched and badly needs: eGGSA'S NEWSPAPER EXTRACTS — the EASTERN PROVINCE HERALD, FORT BEAUFORT ADVOCATE, QUEENSTOWN FREE PRESS, SOUTH AFRICAN COMMERCIAL ADVERTISER and others, transcribed and indexed, with BOOYSEN entries across the 1860s to the 1890s including a Pieter Booysen described as a trek-farmer in 1862. THIS CORRECTS A CONCLUSION DRAWN HOURS EARLIER. Searching 108 million pages of BRITISH papers for this family returned almost nothing, and that was recorded as a limit of the medium. It is not: it is a limit of the COUNTRY. The family's notices are in Cape colonial papers, and those are here, free, and unread.

sets.g: NAAIRS, working again — and KOLBE had never been searched in it
sets.n: a farm, a title, and four records nobody here had
rows: This archive recorded on 13 September that “the bare hostname no longer resolves”. It does — the catalogue is a FRAMESET at national.archives.gov.za/naairs.htm and the SEARCH lives on a DIFFERENT HOST: http://www.national.archsrch.gov.za/sm300cv/smws/sm300dl. Sixteen databases including RSA (all repositories), KAB, TAB, VAB, NAB and GEN, the Genealogical Society's gravestone data. Session-bound URLs, five search boxes with And/Or/Not/Adjacent/Near, and an optional date range. Written down because the wrong address cost this archive a day.

The Kolbes have never been put to NAAIRS. Fourteen rows of searching in September covered Booyzen, Booijzen, Mountjoy, Montjoy, de Beer and Barry — and not once the surname that carries the 1820 Settler, the Conduit Street tailor and the name that runs through this family for four generations. 708 is too many to read; it is recorded as the size of the gap.
Six, and the first is a farm

KAB, source LG, volume 552, system 02, REFERENCE 664, part 1, 1839: “MEMORIALS RECEIVED. LAND. REVEREND G KOLBE. REQUESTING THAT CERTAIN GOVERNMENT GROUND ADJOINING HIS FARM KNAP DAAR IN DISTRICT OF COLESBERG BE SURVEYED AND PUT UP FOR PUBLIC AUCTION.” This archive has George Augustus Kolbe dying at the farm “WURTEMBURG”, Colesberg, on 1 December 1844, and describes him as having preached across the Orange River. Here he is FIVE YEARS EARLIER, formally styled REVEREND, holding a farm called KNAP DAAR and petitioning the government about the ground next door. STRONG BUT NOT PROVED: the memorial gives an initial, not a full name.
The other five of the six

NAB MSCE 414/1960 — Oosthuizen, Pierre Francois, born Colesberg, spouse ADRIANA HENRIETTA JOHANNA, BORN KOLBE, deceased estate. NAB MSCE 131/1959 — BEUKES, PETRONELLA JACOBA ADRIANA, BORN KOLBE, BORN IN COLESBERG, deceased estate. Two Kolbe-born women of Colesberg with estate files, neither in this archive. And two Anglo-Boer War movement permits: VAB SRC volume 7, RC2170, 28 MAY 1901 — “PERMISSION GRANTED FOR MRS. G KOLBE AND CHILD TO PROCEED TO COLESBERG”; and TAB SOPOW volume 39, 1902 — “APPLICATIONS BY JC KOLBE TO PROCEED TO COLESBERG”. SOPOW is the Staff Officer for Prisoners of War, the same series that holds this family's three Booyzen prisoners. The sixth match is a London Missionary Society guide entry and is not a Kolbe document.

sets.g: The Savoy registers, located — and RootsChat, which could not be used
sets.n: an account wall, and a better answer from the National Archives
rows: RootsChat, for the German Lutheran congregations and the Savoy registers

“You are not allowed to search for posts in this forum. Please login below or register an account.” RootsChat's search is closed to visitors, and registering an account is not something this archive does on the user's behalf. NOT SEARCHED. The question it was going to be asked — where the Savoy chapel registers are — turned out to have a better answer somewhere free and citable, so nothing was lost.
The National Archives Discovery catalogue, instead

The registers of the GERMAN LUTHERAN CHURCH, SAVOY, STRAND are at The National Archives in series RG 4, the non-parochial registers surrendered to the Registrar General. DEATHS AND BURIALS: RG 4/4625, RG 4/4626, RG 4/4628, RG 4/4631. BIRTHS AND BAPTISMS: RG 4/4627, RG 4/4629. Two of the eight pieces the catalogue returns are marked available for download. THIS MATTERS DIRECTLY: this archive already cites Johan Gottlieb Kolbe's burial there on 26 November 1845, ENTRY 55, GRAVE 7 — and that entry sits in one of the four Deaths and Burials pieces above. The register it came from now has a reference, and can be checked rather than trusted.

sets.g: The London Gazette — free, and it had a document nobody here had looked for
sets.n: one notice, and it names his trade, his street and his partner
rows: The London Gazette, ISSUE 19424, PAGE 1702, published 29 SEPTEMBER 1836. The OCR is rough and the reading is given cleaned, with the original's damage noted: “TAKE notice, that the Copartnership heretofore subsisting between the undersigned, JOHN GOTTLOB KOLBE and DAVID FLETCHER, of CONDUIT-STREET, BOND-STREET, in the County of MIDDLESEX, TAILORS, has b[een dissolved]…” (the scan gives “Coaftnership”, “Gbttlob” and “t'onduit-Sireet”). FOUR THINGS AT ONCE, from a free and citable printed source: the name in the form JOHN GOTTLOB, matching both the 1803 baptism and the 1845 death registration; the trade TAILOR, which this archive had from the death record alone; CONDUIT STREET in 1836 — five years before the census and nine before he died there; and a BUSINESS PARTNER, DAVID FLETCHER, whom this archive had never heard of.
What the notice does not say

The visible OCR stops at “has b…”. A dissolution notice normally goes on to say from what date, which partner continues the business, and who settles the debts, and both partners sign. None of that has been read: the Gazette's page view is a scanned image rather than text, and the full wording needs the PDF. Recorded as located and part-read, not as read.

sets.g: FreeBMD — never used before, and it had exactly one thing to give
sets.n: the GRO reference for a death this archive already knew the date of
rows: Deaths · surname Kolbe · 1845–1846 · England and Wales
ONE entry, and it is him

“Deaths Dec 1845 — KOLBE, JOHN GOTTLOB — ST GEO HAN SQ — VOL 1, PAGE 35.” The only Kolbe death registered in England and Wales across two years. Three things come off it. The DISTRICT is St George Hanover Square, which is the same registration district the 1841 census gives for Conduit Street, so the census and the death index agree without either knowing about the other. The NAME is entered “JOHN GOTTLOB” — not Johan Gottlieb — which is precisely the form used at his son George Augustus's baptism at St Anne's Soho in 1803, “son of John Gottlob and Mary”. And VOL 1 PAGE 35 is a certificate reference: the certificate itself would give cause of death, occupation, and the NAME AND ADDRESS OF THE INFORMANT, who in a household of three unmarried women is likely to be one of them. NOT ORDERED.
What FreeBMD cannot do for this family, stated so nobody tries

The other London events are all EARLIER and will never be in this index: John Gottlob and Mary at Soho in 1802, George Augustus's baptism at St Anne's in February 1803, and the Shoreditch marriage of 1819. Those are parish records and stay parish records. FreeBMD's entire purchase on this family is the one 1845 death — which is why it took one search, and why it was worth doing.

sets.g: The London end, opened — Kolbe and Downing, not Montjoy
sets.n: four places with prose and no records behind them
rows: What the London places actually are

Worth stating before anyone searches: the four London places on the atlas — ST ANNE'S SOHO, ST LEONARD'S SHOREDITCH, 34 CONDUIT STREET and the GERMAN SAVOY CHURCH — belong to the KOLBE and DOWNING lines, not to the Montjoys. The Montjoy line has no London place at all: James Montjoy is “born Europe about 1782” and his 1840 death notice answers his parents NOT KNOWN. Anyone hoping the London records will reach the Montjoys is looking at the wrong family's city.
The marriage is indexed, three times

Three entries for GEORGE KOLBE, Shoreditch 1819, in ENGLAND MARRIAGES 1538–1973 — two filed under Middlesex and one under London, which is the same event indexed three ways. This archive has read the marriage itself and knows what it says: he was sixteen and she fifteen, both swore they were twenty-one, and she signed with a mark. THE INDEX ADDS NOTHING TO THAT, and is recorded because a place on the atlas with no attached record looks unsearched when it is not.

94 parish records, 255 census, 45 directories, 36 travel — and the ones that surface are Woolwich and Plumstead Kolbes of the 1900s, a Streatham Kolbe of 1881, and passenger lists to the Cape in 1902 and 1957. The Georgian German-tailor Kolbes of Soho and Conduit Street are not what a bare surname search in London returns. They need to be approached by event and parish, not by name.
FindMyPast, as a tool — recorded for whoever comes next

ONE: the results URL takes KeywordsPlace, and a place passed as “placename” is silently ignored — 20,309 results against 12 for the same search. TWO: the NEWSPAPER results URL cannot be reached by parameters at all; /search-newspapers/results?keywords= only works once the form has been clicked, and a direct navigation bounces to the landing page. THREE: result rows resist programmatic clicking, so opening a transcript is a manual step. None of this is a reason not to use it; all of it is a reason to budget more time than the searching itself takes.

“We can't find any matching articles for tolosberg.” The name appears NOWHERE in the British and Irish press. That is a scoped negative with real weight: it explains why the place is in no battle list and no gazetteer, and it means the capture of forty-two Boers with two guns on 25 April 1901 was never reported in Britain under that name. The place is real — a prisoner register and a medal roll both carry it — and the British papers never heard of it.

The Booysen spelling returns 3,262 against Booyzen's 7, and Daschner 42 — all of them modern, British or unrelated. Recorded as a limit of the medium rather than of the search: BRITISH PAPERS DID NOT PRINT THE NAMES OF INDIVIDUAL BOER PRISONERS. The Scheepers charge sheet is the exception because it was a trial. Anyone expecting this family to appear in the British press should expect war reporting and nothing else.
THE HOUSEHOLD, FOUR YEARS BEFORE HE DIED

1841 England census, HO107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, SCHEDULE 38 — St George Hanover Square, sub-district MAY FAIR, street CONDUIT STREET. “JOHN G KOLBE, male, age 76, birth year 1765, birth county as transcribed: FOREIGN.” Two things follow. The archive corrected the family tree's “Lamb's Conduit Street” to 34 Conduit Street from his death record; the census puts him in Conduit Street four years earlier, INDEPENDENTLY. And “FOREIGN” is the first document here to say in its own words that he was not English — the German origin had been an inference off a German church burial. THREE WOMEN share the schedule: MARIANNE, 35, CHARLOTTE, 30, and AMELIA A., 25, none of whom this archive had. No Mary: George Augustus's mother, named at his 1803 baptism, is not in the house.
ONE man in the whole county

HO107 piece 2374, folio 563, page 12, SCHEDULE 46: “JOHN BARRY, Head, MARRIED, male, age 55, birth year 1796, birth town WHITBY, occupation SHIP OWNER, full address SHIP YARDS, RUSWARP, WHITBY.” He is the ONLY John Barry born about 1796 in the 1851 Yorkshire census. The 1838 licence gives a man of the same birth year whose RESIDENCE parish was Bilsdale Midcable — residence, not birth — so a man born at Whitby, living at Bilsdale when he married Margaret Jackson in 1838, and back at Ruswarp by 1851 is one life, not two.

No Barry of any forename is indexed at Bilsdale in either census. The Bilsdale connection rests entirely on the residence parish given on the 1838 marriage licence, which is consistent with a man who lived there briefly and is not evidence of a family seated there. Recorded because “a Yorkshire farmer of Bilsdale” is how the family tree describes him, and the censuses do not support the farm or the seat.
England & Wales Deaths · John Barry · Whitby district

Two John Barry deaths are registered in the WHITBY district, in 1858 and in 1860. Set against the 1851 census, where the county's only John Barry of that age is a Whitby ship owner alive at Ruswarp, the conclusion is plain: THE YORKSHIRE JOHN BARRY BORN 1796 DIED IN YORKSHIRE, AT LEAST FIVE YEARS AFTER THE CAPE MAN DIED AT DE BRUINS POORT IN 1853. Question 6 asked this archive to break one profile holding two men. It is broken — not by finding the Cape man, but by following the Yorkshire man past the date the Cape man died. CAVEAT, and it is a real one: the death index gives no age, so neither Whitby death is tied to him by anything but district and period.
1851 census · Kolbe · Conduit Street, then all London
Gone, and only a governess left

ZERO Kolbes at Conduit Street in 1851 — he had died in 1845 and the household had broken up. In the whole of London in 1851 there is ONE Kolbe: “J Kolbe”, female, unmarried, 25, born London 1826, occupation GOVERNESS, a VISITOR at 4 Camberwell New Road Alfred Place, Lambeth. Too young by a decade to be Marianne, Charlotte or Amelia. The three women of schedule 38 are not in the 1851 London census under their own surname.
Amelia married, and four other Kolbes surface

AMELIA ANN KOLBE married at ST PANCRAS in 1854 — indexed twice, in England & Wales Marriages 1837–2005 and England Marriages 1538–1973. That is the Amelia A. of the 1841 Conduit Street schedule, aged 25 there and marrying thirteen years later. Four others, none tied to this family and all recorded so the next person does not have to find them again: EMANUEL CHRISTOPHER KOLBE, BORN 1766, buried at Bermondsey St Mary Magdalen 1836 — one year younger than Johan Gottlieb and worth testing as a brother; GEORGE KOLBE, died 1848, Westminster St Margaret; ELIZABETH KOLBE, died 1852, Strand; and JANE DAY KOLBE, in the London Gazette in 1852 and married in 1853.
A lead that does NOT need a subscription
J. G. Kolbe in the London Gazette, 1836
